## Using the renv package

renv is a package-management package, in that it stores packages relative to the R project instead of the computer. 
- Info is written into a lockfile, which is uploaded to git
- This installs relevant packages and the version used when creating the original project

```{r Part 1: Loading Necessary Packages}
library (ggplot2)
library (dplyr)
library(paletteer)

```
## Additional renv Notes

In the console, write renv::init. This downloads all packages, shows Rstudio and package versions, and creates a lock file and folder for the lock file.

- The .gitignore is the file stating that we don't want git tracking these packages; we don't want this because it keeps us from repeating installation
- renv::restore brings all the packages back that are being kept in the lockfile


## Optional Material - RMoCap package
 
I chose to look into the RMoCap package because my lab relies on motion capture as a form of gait and movement analysis. Personally, I have used software such as OpenSim and OpenCap in the past, and may use it in the future. I would like to have a better understanding of this package so I can use it for future studies and data analysis.
